findings.title: Auth lifecycle revocation sentence should distinguish central account from external tenant Auth
evidence: docs/gridex-staff-api.md:53 immediately after independent binding instructions broadly says banning/deleting user in Auth ends access next request
lib/staff-api/context.ts:163-186 checks signed proof, current binding and native central membership; no tenant Auth bearer/getUser port
supabase/migrations/20261004085008_staff_active_membership.sql:12-19 joins central auth.users banned/deleted state
lib/staff-api/tenantAuth.ts:68-82 remote tenant getUser/lifecycle runs in onboarding resolve/accept only
findings.proof: Normal independent Staff operations require proof and binding claims, not x-gridex-support-auth-token. Native guard has no remote tenant Auth connection. Central account ban/delete revokes immediately; remote local Auth ban/deletion prevents successful new resolve/accept, but does not by itself invalidate an already-issued fresh-JTI Staff proof.
findings.impact: Documentation can lead operators to rely on tenant Auth revocation alone for immediate ordinary Staff API refusal. Trusted tenant backend is expected to verify its staff and stop signing after revocation.
findings.targeted_fix: Clarify that next-request native ban/delete checks apply central Gridex actor; tenant backend must verify current local Auth before issuing Staff assertions; remote Auth is rechecked on resolve/accept and central disable/binding revocation is authoritative. Do not claim cross-database atomic revocation.
findings.fp_check: No confirmed security bypass against specified current binding/native membership model; documentation overstatement/ambiguity, not evidence that binding disable/revocation fails.
